definitions.explanation: The fifth grade in the {段|だん} ranking system used in martial arts, board games like {碁|ご} (Go) and {将棋|しょうぎ} (shogi), and traditional arts.
In Japanese grammar, a class of verbs whose endings shift across all five rows of the {五十音|ごじゅうおん} table when conjugated. Examples include {書|か}く, {読|よ}む, and {話|はな}す.

examples.japanese: ⟦{柔道|じゅうどう}→柔道：01612_juudou⟧{五段|ごだん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{習|なら}った→習う：00479_narau⟧。
examples.english: I trained under a fifth-dan judo instructor.

examples.japanese: ⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{書道|しょどう}→書道：04178_shodou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{五段|ごだん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取得|しゅとく}した→取得する：10444_shutokusuru⟧。
examples.english: My father obtained the fifth dan in calligraphy.

examples.japanese: ⟦{剣道|けんどう}→剣道：04452_kendou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{五段|ごだん}{昇段|しょうだん}⟦{審査|しんさ}→審査：08375_shinsa⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{技術|ぎじゅつ}→技術：01389_gijutsu⟧⟦だけでなく→〜だけでなく：18373_dakedenaku⟧⟦{人格|じんかく}→人格：11427_jinkaku⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{問|と}われる→問う：02299_tou⟧。
examples.english: The fifth-dan promotion exam in kendo evaluates not only technique but also character.

examples.japanese: 「⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧」⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{五段|ごだん}⟦{動詞|どうし}→動詞：03472_doushi⟧だ。
{五段|ごだん}⟦{動詞|どうし}→動詞：03472_doushi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{活用|かつよう}→活用：02620_katsuyou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}くて→多い：01127_ooi⟧⟦{覚|おぼ}え→覚える：00739_oboeru⟧にくい。
examples.english: Godan verbs are hard to memorize because they have many conjugations.

examples.japanese: {五段|ごだん}⟦{動詞|どうし}→動詞：03472_doushi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{一段|いちだん}→一段：08951_ichidan⟧⟦{動詞|どうし}→動詞：03472_doushi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{違|ちが}い→違い：03432_chigai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{理解|りかい}する→理解する：06059_rikaisuru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦{文法|ぶんぽう}→文法：01506_bunpou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{基礎|きそ}→基礎：03981_kiso⟧だ。
examples.english: Understanding the difference between godan and ichidan verbs is fundamental to Japanese grammar.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{五|ご}→五：00697_go⟧ (five) + ⟦{段|だん}→段：03424_dan⟧ (step, grade, rank).

MEANING 1 — MARTIAL ARTS/GAMES RANKING:
- ⟦{柔道|じゅうどう}→柔道：01612_juudou⟧{五段|ごだん}: fifth dan in judo
- ⟦{剣道|けんどう}→剣道：04452_kendou⟧{五段|ごだん}: fifth dan in kendo
- ⟦{将棋|しょうぎ}→将棋：04172_shougi⟧{五段|ごだん}: fifth dan in shogi
- {五段|ごだん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧: to attain fifth dan
In most disciplines the dan ranks run from 1 (⟦{初段|しょだん}→初段：28129_shodan⟧) up to 10 ({十段|じゅうだん}), with {五段|ごだん} representing a senior practitioner.

MEANING 2 — GRAMMAR:
- {五段|ごだん}⟦{動詞|どうし}→動詞：03472_doushi⟧: godan verb
- {五段|ごだん}⟦{活用|かつよう}→活用：02620_katsuyou⟧: godan conjugation
Named because the verb stem's final consonant takes vowels from all five rows (あいうえお) of the ⟦{五十音|ごじゅうおん}→五十音：15489_gojuuon⟧ table during conjugation. Contrast with ⟦{一段|いちだん}→一段：08951_ichidan⟧⟦{動詞|どうし}→動詞：03472_doushi⟧ (ichidan verbs), whose stems stay on a single row.
